rounds.proof_sketch: With blockDim.x=256, at s=1, original has tid<1 (thread 0 works), mutated has tid<0 (no threads work). The final max reduction step shared_max[0]=max(shared_max[0],shared_max[1]) is skipped. Thread 1 processes positions 1,257,513,... If max is only in thread 1's range, row_max is wrong.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes thread participation at the boundary of each reduction stage, most critically at s=1 where the final comparison between shared_max[0] and shared_max[1] is completely eliminated. This means any maximum value located in features processed exclusively by thread 1 (positions 1, 257, 513, etc.) will not be properly reduced into the final row_max. When an extreme value exists in thread 1's range, the mutant uses an incorrect (smaller) max, causing numerical overflow in the exp() calculation.
rounds.kill_strategy: Place a large value (e.g., 500.0) at position 1 which is exclusively processed by thread 1, while keeping thread 0's positions at 0. The mutant will compute row_max=0 instead of 500, causing exp(500) overflow.
rounds.recommendations: Parallel reduction boundary conditions are critical and subtle. Test with data distributions where maximum/minimum values are located at positions corresponding to different threads in the reduction tree to verify correct propagation through all reduction stages.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    x = torch.zeros(16, 16384, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    # Position 1 is processed by thread 1, not thread 0
    # Mutant's broken reduction won't propagate this max to shared_max[0]
    x[:, 1] = 500.0  # Causes exp(500) overflow in mutant
    return [x]
